what_it_does: 3D Gaussian Splatting is a technique for reconstructing and rendering 3D scenes by representing everything as a cloud of fuzzy blobs (Gaussians) rather than triangles — training this representation is currently painfully slow due to three distinct memory bottlenecks. First, large blobs that cover many pixels are loaded from off-chip main memory (DRAM — the large, slow memory chip in a computer) repeatedly for every pixel they touch, causing redundant slow fetches. Second, during the learning 'backward pass' (the step where the system adjusts its parameters based on errors), many gradient values (tiny correction signals) must be added to shared running totals using costly 'atomic' operations that force each update to wait its turn. Third, reading intermediate results from the fast on-chip memory suffers 'bank conflicts' — multiple reads trying to access the same memory bank at the same moment and being forced to queue. GSArch adds three targeted hardware fixes: a smart on-chip cache for frequently-used large blobs, a filter that skips low-value gradient updates, and a memory-access rearranging unit that avoids simultaneous bank conflicts.
